name: loop-dynamics
description: passive loop-filter bandwidth / phase margin over the 27-bundle passive corner box x temperature x Vctrl, with a whole-loop AC cross-check
claim: #4/#8/#9 -> #10 (design-input claim, not a spec line) -- DR-001 Decision 1's fixed second-order loop filter (series R + shunt C1 + shunt C2, design/loop_filter.sch) meets an explicit phase-margin criterion (>= 45 deg) and the f_c < f_ref/10 sampled-loop ceiling at every point of the PVT x Kvco-spread x N=4-64 x Icp-trim cross-product, using #8's extracted Kvco(Vctrl) table and #9's Icp/trim data; plus C1's real area against the 0.15 mm^2 budget and the ripple-vs-lock-time tradeoff.
methodology: **Exact reduction, not an approximation.** For the type-II charge-pump loop of DR-001 Decision 1, T(s) = (Icp/2pi)*Z(s)*(2pi*Kvco/s)/N = A*Z(s)/s with A = Icp*Kvco/N, so Icp, Kvco and N enter ONLY through the scalar A. One measured filter impedance curve per (passive corner, temperature, Vctrl) point therefore covers the ENTIRE Kvco x N x Icp-trim x f_ref cross-product for that filter corner exactly. The A axis is still swept on a dense log grid between its measured extremes (see `analyze.py`), so no unimodality assumption is relied on.

**Reduction is the baseline's own.** `testbench/derive.py` rebuilds the two CSVs the pre-migration `run.sh` stitched together with awk from the deck's `wrdata` files and calls `testbench/analyze.py` with only its entry point made callable; the algebra is unchanged. R, C1 and C2 are MEASURED from each Z(jw) curve's asymptotes and phase peak (a 3-element fit), not drawn values.

**Independent cross-check.** The `d<k><t|s|f>` points re-simulate the WHOLE linearized loop (phase-domain behavioural PFD/CP, VCO and divider around the real filter) at 18 real (Icp, Kvco, N) design points -- six reference-frequency decades at each of the typical (`rtyp-mtyp-xtyp`, 27 C, Vctrl 1.8 V), slow (`rss-mss-xss`, -40 C, 0.9 V) and fast (`rff-mff-xff`, 125 C, 2.7 V) filter corners. Their Icp and Kvco come from the pinned #9/#8 tables via `pick_xcheck.py`; a unit test checks the manifest's numbers against that script's output.

**One fragment, two benches.** The pre-migration campaign had two decks (`tb_loop_filter_ac.sp`, `tb_loop_ac.sp`). sim/harness runs one deck per grid point and `phases` would run both at every point (81 x 6 cross-check runs instead of 18), so the benches share one fragment, share no node, and the `run` sweep axis (`z` or `d<k><t|s|f>`) selects which output a point reads and over which `grid` block it runs. 81 filter runs + 18 cross-check points = 99, the baseline grid.

**Criteria applied** (stated up front): phase margin >= 45 deg everywhere in the operating space (this campaign's adopted criterion -- DR-001 states none); f_c < f_ref/10, the sampled-loop stability ceiling DR-001 Decision 1 names; small-signal 1 % settling < 100 us (draft lock-time target, 20 us stretch); C1 area against the draft 0.15 mm^2 block budget. The 0.3 V Vctrl point is below the DR-003 window: characterized for the C-V check only, excluded from the stability cross-product. (f_ref, N) pairs whose f_out falls outside the ratified 10-200 MHz band are excluded, not reported as failures.

**Band-selection rule is load-bearing (DR-003 Decision 4):** Kvco is taken under the rule that a correctly configured part selects the LOWEST band that reaches the target f_out; the adversarial-band Kvco is not part of the cross-product.

**DUT pinned to the baseline's frozen export.** `design/netlist/loop_filter.spice` on `main` has since moved C2 to `cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield` (option-B MIM); the baseline record measured `cap_mim_2f0_m2m3_noshield`. To measure the harness/simulator delta and nothing else, this manifest composes the baseline record's own netlist snapshot (`sim/loop-dynamics/netlist-snapshots/20260731-202550-82af5a9.spice`, SHA-256 e4c2184f...) rather than the live export. A run against the current export is a different claim and needs its own record.

**Axes not swept:** MOS process bundles (tt/ff/ss/fs/sf) N/A -- the filter contains no active device (MOS typical is composed but unused); supply N/A -- neither the filter nor the impedance bench has a supply node (a single nominal supply point is run, `supply_tolerance` = 0). The cross-check's behavioural PFD/CP and VCO are ideal and carry no PVT dependence of their own. The process axis IS the passive box: 27 bundles of `res_{typical,ff,ss}` x `moscap_{typical,ff,ss}` x `mimcap_{typical,ff,ss}`, named `r<res>-m<moscap>-x<mimcap>`. Because the mandated matrix (five MOS bundles, three supplies) does not apply to this DUT, a recorded run needs `--subset-reason`.

**Limitations:** small-signal (nominal skew, `sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0`, no Monte Carlo); lock time is a small-signal estimate from the fitted model's dominant closed-loop pole (cycle slipping and large-signal VCO behaviour are #12's); schematic-level, no parasitics (#18).

**Cross-record comparability (simulator / host delta).** The baseline `20260731-202550-82af5a9` was taken with ngspice-46 on Darwin 25.6.0 / arm64; harness runs on this project's Linux hosts use ngspice on Linux x86_64. The record's own Environment provenance states the simulator, host(s) and backend of THIS run and is authoritative. The `baseline_comparison` table is the pilot go/no-go gate: every metric against the baseline with the ratified tolerance, none loosened.
